houseViews.view: Maintained: the freeze deepens and the stratification is now conclusive. Sydney Northwest remains the pure strike — 33.6 months, only 197 of 580 listings priced (34%), asking $2,420/m² against $2,342 on the thin priced tail. Sydney Southwest holds a +39% ask-to-sold gap ($2,101 vs $1,511) at 29.6 months. The decisive print is Sydney South West: honestly priced ($2,200 vs $2,087, a 5% gap) yet months-stock worsened 33.7→35.2 on just 263 annual sales — at $725k medians, honest pricing does not clear; only a demand shock or a price level shift does. NSW headline 15.3→15.6 months confirms the state is re-loosening as actives build 3,227→3,296.
houseViews.falsifier: Basin priced-share rising above 60% (Northwest especially) alongside corridor months-stock falling below 20 on rising sold counts.

houseViews.view: Maintained with a caution flag: VIC is still the only major market where the overhang builds daily — 17.1 months, actives 6,585→6,650 — and still the only deep market that is screenable (95% priced, $395k median). But the ask-to-sold gap has widened to 16% ($843 vs $728/m²) from the 13% we carried, and Melbourne North is now at 21.0 months on 485 sales. The mechanical case holds — cheap, abundant, priced stock is where the late-2026 investor rotation lands — but the widening gap says fringe vendors are starting to price hope, which delays absorption. Overhang caps price, rotation rescues volume; watch the gap, not the median.
houseViews.falsifier: VIC months-stock pushing past 20 with sold 12m rolling below ~4,000, ask-to-sold gap widening past 20%, or new-listing absorption failing to lift by Q1 2027.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the demand desert persists an hour past the fringe — Melbourne Peri-Urban 38.2 months on 126 annual sales, South Gippsland 33.1 on 100, Gippsland 26.2 on 66, West Gippsland 20.5 on 146. Ask-to-sold gaps of 13–25% ($576 vs $511 Peri-Urban, $628 vs $504 South Gippsland) on top of no volume means these are not overpriced markets, they are markets without buyers: with fringe lots at $395k and 17 months of metro choice, the 644–772m² lifestyle lot has no scarcity premium. Avoid englobo and stage stock; this belt clears last, after the fringe digests.
houseViews.falsifier: Belt sold volumes rising 50%+ per window, or peri-urban months-stock falling below 25 without listings simply being withdrawn.

houseViews.market: Regional VIC hubs vs fallen-angel prints (Ballarat/Bendigo)
houseViews.view: Maintained: trust the corridor, not the 7-sale suburb print. Bendigo suburb still tops the fallen angels at -37.6% — on 7 sales with lot sizes simultaneously down 37.1%, pure mix — while the Bendigo corridor clears 301 annual sales at 9.6 months and Ballarat 456 at 10.2, both far tighter than VIC's 17.1. At $315–325k these hubs are the cheapest functioning volume markets in the state, absorbing the buyer the fringe cannot serve at $410–440k. The real regional weakness stays in low-volume satellites: Creswick -36.8% 3yr on 8 sales, Smythesdale -22.2% on 5.
houseViews.falsifier: Ballarat/Bendigo corridor months-stock rising above 14, or corridor sold $/m² printing negative on stable 250+ sale windows.

houseViews.view: Updated: the capitulation-clears thesis holds but the watch-name changes. Torquay's bottoming is on track (-13.5% prior year → -5.9% last 12m on 43 sales vs 9 three years ago). The new tell is St Leonards: -11.3% last 12m on 55 sales — the highest-volume decline in the fallen-angel set, meaning this is genuine repricing that is actually transacting, the healthy version of the adjustment. The holdouts remain Portarlington (-25.6% 3yr on 10 sales) and San Remo (-25.9% on 15) where thin volume says vendors haven't met the market; they have another leg down. Pakenham's -23.6% 3yr is mostly mix (lots +62%).
houseViews.falsifier: Torquay/St Leonards volumes falling back below ~15-20 per window, or price declines re-accelerating past -10% in the priced coastal names.

houseViews.view: Maintained with rising conviction: the sold base is up 10.4% in 30 days (10,069→11,114) while months-stock fell 13.7→13.5 into a 9% listings build (11,497→12,540) — absorption outrunning supply is the early-positioning footprint ahead of the 1 Jul 2027 changes (negative gearing narrowed to new builds, CGT discount replaced by indexation). The bid lands where product is priced and cheap — VIC (95% priced, $395k), QLD corridors, SA — not Sydney basins where 66% of Northwest stock cannot be screened. Tight markets (SA 6.4, Adelaide North 5.4) take it as price; loose priced markets take it as volume.
houseViews.falsifier: No pickup in investor-share of land sales or VIC/QLD new-listing absorption by Q1 2027, or policy amendment before commencement.

houseViews.view: Maintained: still the tightest mainland market but loosening at the margin — 6.1→6.3→6.4 months over 30 days with actives 479→540 (+13%). Adelaide North remains a zero-negotiation market ($914 asking vs $910 sold at 5.4 months). The headline ~28% sold-$/m² growth stays composition-inflated (one estate ≈ a third of 2026 sales; like-for-like ≈ +9.5%), and the $420k median is defended almost entirely via lot compression (Roseworthy -47% 3yr, Mount Barker -27.2%, Morphett Vale -32.6%) — compression is the market's confession that the gross-price ceiling binds. Path remains deceleration, not correction, with the 2027 rotation delaying the reckoning.
houseViews.falsifier: Stock above 10 months, incentive share rising two runs in a row, or lot compression stalling while sales volumes fall.

houseViews.view: Maintained at high conviction: the blow-off signature is complete — $/m² accelerated +52.2% then +96.3% to $1,027 (vs $344 three years ago) while lots compressed another 38% in one year and volume thinned 79→46→34 per window. A market that doubles its rate while shrinking the product a third on falling volume is borrowing from the ceiling, not raising it; at $1,027/m² the compressed lot still prints a $400k+ gross in a market whose whole premise is sub-$450k affordability. Sell stage stock into this rate; do not underwrite englobo at these residuals.
houseViews.falsifier: Lot sizes stabilising while $/m² keeps rising on volume recovering above ~50 sales per window.

houseViews.view: Updated — the collision we flagged has produced its first casualty print: months-stock rose 7.9→8.2 as actives built 607→756 (+25% in 30 days, the fastest of any state) against a 20% forward-priced gap ($1,041 asked vs $867 sold) and only 69% of stock priced. Mandurah is the state in miniature: +98.6% last 12m with lots -35% 3yr on thinning volume (40→33→22), while Hilbert and Australind second-derivatives fade (59.3→27.8%, 53.1→43.3%). The unpriceable prints elsewhere persist — Greenbank +56.6% to $1,373/m² on 6 sales (from 76), Virginia +72.9% on 8 (from 48) — sell-out selection, not demand; treat any sub-15-sale window as noise against Mount Barker's real +64.6% on 89 sales.
houseViews.falsifier: WA months-stock stabilising below 9 on the next two runs (turn was noise), or breaching 10 (turn confirmed, escalate to underweight); Greenbank/Virginia volumes recovering above ~20 per window with $/m² holding.

houseViews.view: Updated: the contamination thesis is confirmed and the series is now stabilising at its new base — asking $478k→$479k, $/m² $710→$721, actives 1,056→1,071 over 24 hours, exactly the flat-lining you'd expect once the 7-Jul universe expansion (948→1,022 suburbs) washed through rather than genuine repricing. Underlying market remains firm at 9.1 months: South Ripley +82% last 12m to $1,774/m² on a 33-sale window, Bahrs Scrub +53% to $1,319 on stable 16–23 sale windows. The new $479k/9.1-month base is now usable as a level; the 30-day change series stays quarantined until August.
houseViews.falsifier: Like-for-like (pre-expansion suburb set) QLD asking or sold $/m² actually falling on the next monthly comparison, or the new base failing to hold ±3% over the next fortnight.
